headline: Japan: Yen strengthens on possibility of consecutive rate hikes, fears of 'yen carry trade unwinding'
summary: The yen surged on the 3rd, briefly reaching the 157-per-dollar range for the first time in a month, as the possibility of consecutive Bank of Japan rate hikes came into focus. Reports cite fears of a yen carry trade unwinding.
why: The Bank of Japan sets interest rates for Japan, and yen moves affect global carry trades, where investors borrow cheaply in yen to fund higher-yielding assets.
why_moved: Possible consecutive Bank of Japan rate hikes boosted the yen, and fears of a carry trade unwinding added to the move.
